effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (SDLI-EN010, Realm of Light Structure Deck)

changes.historical_text: Cannot be Normal Summoned or Set. When this card is sent from your Deck to the Graveyard: Special Summon it.
changes.modern_text: Cannot be Normal Summoned/Set. Must be Special Summoned by a card effect, and cannot be Special Summoned by other ways. If this card is sent from your Deck to the Graveyard: Special Summon it.
changes.summary: Functional erratum: SDLI-EN010 added "Must be Special Summoned by a card effect, and cannot be Special Summoned by other ways". The modern script encodes it as an EFFECT_SPSUMMON_CONDITION (EFFECT_FLAG_CANNOT_DISABLE+EFFECT_FLAG_UNCOPYABLE) whose value function accepts a Special Summon only when its source effect IsHasType(EFFECT_TYPE_ACTIONS) - an activate, ignition, trigger or quick effect. The pre-errata script registers no summon restriction whatsoever, so any Special Summon of Wulf is legal, including ones performed by continuous effects or by Summoning procedures rather than by an activated card effect. Both keep c:EnableUnsummonable() and the identical mandatory TRIGGER_F on EVENT_TO_GRAVE that revives it when it is sent from the Deck to the Graveyard.

review.notes: The earlier transition v0 (LODT-EN023, 2008-05-13) -> v1 (LCGX-EN248, 2011-10-04) precedes the baseline's recorded version and is cosmetic PSCT: "This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set. When this card is sent from your Deck to the Graveyard, Special Summon it." -> "Cannot be Normal Summoned or Set. ... to the Graveyard: Special Summon it." v0 is the text in force at the Edison snapshot (2010-04-24) and resolves identically; the baseline cdb text matches v1 (packet ratio 0.9463, differing only in "Normal Summoned/Set" vs "Normal Summoned or Set"). The card postdates the GOAT snapshot (first TCG printing 2008-05-13). Trailing v2 -> v3 (BLLR-EN039, 2017-07-06) drops the redundant "and cannot be Special Summoned by other ways" and modernises Graveyard to GY: cosmetic, not recorded. EdisonFormat's Lightsworn entry concerns phase-dependent mandatory Trigger Effects re-activating after their activation is negated; Wulf's revival trigger is event-based (sent from Deck to Graveyard), so that entry does not bear on this record and is not cited.
